properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22: "While some designs are not testable by an agent (say a user designs a house, the agent can't test that, but an agent can test code). In both cases, results of testing can be provided back to reflow2 and the reflow2 design can capture that feedback and see how the design needs to change."

⭐ THE MECHANISM IS BUILT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. `reconcile_verification` exists and its own description calls it "the P4 reconcile, LAST OF THE THREE FEEDBACK LOOPS (BL-30)". You hand it what a run reported per check; a recorded `passing` that the run FAILED "is the dangerous direction and sorts first — the design believed proven what is actually broken"; with `record_events` each divergence becomes a persistent DriftEvent that auto-resolves when a later run agrees. That is his sentence, implemented.

🛑 AND ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN IT HAS LEFT NO TRACE: 311 checks `passing`, **0 ever `failing`**, no verification DriftEvent. The loop is complete and has never been closed. Nothing requires it, nothing reports its absence, so it is never called — the same opt-in shape as every other leg of the chain.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. The first three are about making it FIRE; the fourth is the case he raised that none of them covers.

(a) THE RUN FEEDS ITSELF BACK. `req:a-ci-run-leaves-a-machine-readable-record-of-what-it-ran` is already ACCEPTED (2026-09-21) and produces the file; a step maps gate → Verification and calls `reconcile_verification` with it. ⭐ Turns every green build into evidence and every red build into a DriftEvent, with no session remembering anything. ⚠️ Counter: the mapping is hand-kept and would drift — it needs an unmapped gate reported loudly, never skipped.

(b) THE LOOP ASKS. `loop_status` already says what is owed; it could say "N checks claim passing and no run has confirmed one in M days". ⭐ Cheap, and it makes the absence visible where somebody is already looking. ⚠️ Counter: another nag on a surface that already has several, and it reports rather than fixes.

(c) A CHECK WITHOUT A RUN DECAYS. A `passing` that nothing has re-run for long enough stops counting as passing in the rollups — not falsified, just no longer evidence. ⚠️ Counter: needs a clock and a threshold nobody has chosen, and this project has a standing objection to thresholds it cannot justify.

⭐ (d) THE NON-AGENT CASE, WHICH IS THE ONE HE ACTUALLY RAISED AND THE ONE NONE OF THE ABOVE COVERS. A house inspection, a pressure test, a beamline alignment, a user saying "this does not work" — the tester is a PERSON, the result arrives as a sentence, and there is no run to reconcile against. Today that person's finding has no path in: `reconcile_verification` wants machine outcomes, and the honest alternative is a human writing a Verification by hand, which is exactly the unfalsifiable record this design already has 282 of.
    THE SHAPE WORTH EXPLORING: a result carries WHO OBSERVED IT and HOW (a run, an inspection, a witness), so "proven by a passing CI gate" and "proven because Anthony looked at it" are both recordable and never confused. `Verification.method` already declares analysis / demonstration / inspection / measurement / observation / review / simulation / test — so the vocabulary is, once again, already there and unused for this.
    ⚠️ Counter: reflow2 must not start judging whether a human's inspection was any good; `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` holds. The goal is to make the BASIS visible, not to rank it.

═══ 2026-09-22 (late) — WHAT STEP 4 NOW ANSWERS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT ═══
Option (a)'s hard part is built, WITHOUT the hand-kept mapping its counter feared: `reconcile_verification` takes a run BY FILE (`observed_by_file`), resolved through each check's `location` or the Artifact that IMPLEMENTS it, and names every unmapped file (cap:a-real-run-is-fed-back-by-file). `tools/test_run_to_files.py` turns cargo output, JUnit XML and script exit codes into that list. And a recorded run now leaves a stamp even when it agrees (dec:a-reconcile-stamps-every-check-it-compared), with loop_status saying whether any result has ever come back (cap:the-loop-closure-reading) — that is option (b), built. STILL OPEN: nothing calls it automatically (CI cannot write the live design), and (d), the person-as-tester, is not addressed — a person can report an outcome by check id, but the stamp records WHAT the run said, not WHO observed it or HOW.

═══ 2026-09-25 — ANTHONY ANSWERS THE PERSON HALF (dev_reflow2 hub session) ═══
"On the human supplied results, if we are discussing flo2.io, the results can be uploaded directly in flo2.io OR via the AI chat + upload documents or simply type test results/feedback into chat. If we are discussing reflow2 being used locally, a user can either provide feedback or test results via a chat (like I'm doing now) or put documentation in some folder and point the agent at its path."

So the routes for a PERSON's results are: hosted — upload on flo2.io, attach documents in the chat, or type them into the chat; local — say them in the session, or put documents in a folder and point the agent at it. Recorded as req:a-person-feeds-results-back-by-upload-chat-or-folder. STILL OPEN from this question: what makes an AUTOMATED run fire back without anyone remembering.
properties.name: OPEN — the tool that feeds a test result back into the design exists and has never been used here. What makes it fire, and what is the path when the tester is a PERSON inspecting a house rather than a CI run?
properties.rationale: Recorded because the reflex answer — "build a way to feed test results back" — would rebuild `reconcile_verification`, which is the fourth time this project would have rebuilt something it already served. The real questions are what makes it fire without a session remembering, and what the path is for a tester who is a person rather than a process; only the second needs anything new, and even there the method vocabulary already exists.
